git-exec.name: Git Exec
git-exec.description: Thin, READ-ONLY wrappers over git (merge-base, rev-parse, commit meta, merge-tree). ABSORB materializes a ref's tree via `git archive | tar` into a temp dir — NO worktree, no .git/worktrees lock — so absorbs run concurrently (T-2026-06-23-003). worktreeAdd/Remove remain only for the cold git<2.38 merge-tree fallback, which needs real merge machinery and is serialized per-repo via #repo-lock. gitUserName reads `git config user.name` (read-only) to seed the default ACTOR of a fabric #pick — coexistence only, never written back. The user's HEAD/index/worktree are never touched.

repo-lock.name: Repo Lock
repo-lock.description: A per-repo, in-process async mutex (withRepoLock(repoRoot, fn)). Serializes the one remaining git-worktree user — the cold git<2.38 merge-tree fallback — per resolved repo root so concurrent calls can't race the .git/worktrees lock; distinct repos run free. A predecessor's rejection never blocks later callers. In-process only (cross-process would need a .git flock; the parallel-absorb path no longer needs a worktree at all).

canonical-json.name: Canonical Json
canonical-json.description: Strict, dependency-free canonical serializer (sorted keys, NFC strings, no whitespace ambiguity) that produces the byte stream the essence hash digests.

essence-hash.name: Essence Hash
essence-hash.description: The load-bearing wall — essence(symbol) -> contentId. Hashes the Canonical Normal Form ⟨kind, normalized contract, edgeBag⟩, Merkle by TARGET essence (so rename is free), excludes name/path/prose/timestamps. Tarjan SCC for cycles; stable-id fold for generic-contract aliasing. .purpose contentId = "essence:v0:" + sha256(canonical). STAGE 3a: a code-unit branch in localCNF (detected by componentType==='code-unit') replaces the sorted edgeBag with the CCNF body and SUBSTITUTES each positional f:N token INLINE with the essence of codeLocalTargets[N]'s edge (via the SAME edgeEssence resolver, so intra-SCC targets become @scc-internal and a cross-symbol rename frees the chain); extern/builtin free:name tokens stay untouched; edgeBag is []. The version tag is read off entry.data.essenceTag (default ESSENCE_VERSION) so a code-unit contentId is "essence:v1:ts<exact>:"+sha256(canonical) and SCC members carry the same tag — mixed v0/v1 graphs interoperate because Merkle substitutes the target's full TAGGED string. essence-hash never imports the lens; the tag travels on the node.

warp-object.name: Warp Object
warp-object.description: A WarpObject — a SymbolEntry stripped of labels and reduced to ⟨kind, contract, sorted outgoing edges, contentId⟩. liftEdges derives outgoing, typed, deduped, sorted edges from the live SymbolIndex (the single edge source the essence hash agrees on).

warp-state.name: Warp State
warp-state.description: A WarpState — the whole symbol graph of one ref lifted to MEANING. stateId = sha256 over the sorted contentIds; treeSha/absorbedAt are provenance, not identity. WarpObject.filePath is normalized REPO-RELATIVE to the absorb root (temp-worktree or cwd, with macOS /private↔/var alias handling) so a path-prefix difference never masquerades as a rename.

warp-store.name: Warp Store
warp-store.description: Content-addressed store for WARP objects + states and the .warpline/oracle.jsonl ledger appender. In-mem primary with a .warpline/ disk cache; loadState(stateId) rehydrates a persisted state back from .warpline/states/ (the Phase-2 write path needs the PARENT state across CLI runs when the in-mem map is cold) — faithful because diff reads only stableKey/contentId/contract, all preserved by serializeState. The ONLY thing Warpline writes to disk is under .warpline/.

code-lens.name: Code Lens
code-lens.description: The TS code-lens interface surface (spec §2 / warpline-code-lens.md). Types ONLY (stage 1): CodeUnit — a SymbolEntry-shaped synthetic node keyed #code:<rel-path>::<qualified-name>, carrying the identity-bearing codeEssence (CCNF) body slot, resolved free-reference edges, and a visible reducedFidelity marker — and the CodeLens registry contract (extensions + lift()). Declares no behavior; pins the shape the lift machinery (ts-lens, stage 2) is built against. componentType 'code-unit' lets code-units flow through the EXISTING WARP (essence-hash/sem-delta/predict/oracle) as nodes in the same universe, never a parallel graph.

code-essence.name: Code Essence
code-essence.description: The pure-syntactic Code Canonical Normal Form (CCNF) producer — codeCNF(node) -> canonical token string for one declaration. The SYNTACTIC HALF of the lens: structure + WRITTEN annotations only, NO ts.Program/checker. Hardens the AST-absorb spike: (1) scope-correct alpha-normalization honoring JS hoisting (var/fn-decl -> nearest function scope; let/const/class -> block; params/type-params -> unit scope; catch var -> catch scope) with bindings as (depth, ordinal) coordinates and shadowing-correct use resolution, replacing the spike's unsound flat first-declaration-order map; (2) separate b:/t:/L: namespaces (the spike ignored type-params, so f<T> vs f<U> falsely DIFFERed); (3) the false-EQUAL guard (§3.2) — async/generator*/static/readonly/abstract/ get-set/optional?/default-presence/rest.../definite!/optional-chain?./nullish?? each produce a DISTINCT cnf; (4) literal normalization (§3.3) — integers (hex/oct/bin) -> exact decimal, bigint -> decimal+n, non-integer numerics -> raw source lexeme NOT an IEEE-754 round-trip (0.1 != 1e-1 by design), strings/templates NFC; (5) directive comments (@ts-ignore/@ts-expect-error/ @ts-nocheck/eslint-disable) hashed, free prose dropped. An optional freeRefClassifier strips free names to positional f:{idx} edge tokens (default emits free:{name}, keeping stage 1 self-contained and spike-equivalent). Stage 2 adds codeCNFDetailed(node,opts) -> {cnf, freeRefs[]}: the SAME first-appearance ordering drives both the body's f:{idx} tokens and the freeRefs index, so freeRefs[idx] (name + a representative ts.Identifier node) aligns 1:1 with the f:idx token. codeCNF now delegates to it and returns .cnf (the stage-1 signature is unchanged). This positional alignment is the input the lens hands the checker for §4 resolution; call order is meaning, so a sorted edge-set would be wrong.

code-symbol.name: Code Symbol
code-symbol.description: Pure string builders for a code-unit's WARP key and structural stable key (spec §2). codeSymbol(relPath, qualifiedName) -> "#code:"+relPath+"::"+ qualifiedName (the SymbolIndex key); codeStableKey(relPath, structuralPath) -> relPath+"::"+structuralPath where structuralPath is the (scopeKind#ordinal) chain (e.g. class#0/method#2). Both are LABELS — provenance + rename tiebreakers — NEVER hashed; pure functions of their inputs (no I/O), so trivially deterministic across machines.

ts-lens.name: Ts Lens
ts-lens.description: The TS/TSX code-lens (stage 2, spec §4/§5) — the checker-dependent half. TsLens.lift(rootDir) enumerates .ts/.tsx files (sorted, .d.ts excluded), builds ONE ts.Program over them against a FIXED, HARDCODED compiler-options baseline (ESNext target/module, Bundler resolution, strict, skipLibCheck, noEmit, allowJs:false — NEVER a discovered tsconfig, §5.2), and lifts each code-unit (FunctionDeclaration, arrow/fn-expr const, class + its method/ctor/ getter/setter/field members; default-export -> qualifiedName 'default'; overload sets -> the implementation signature, bodiless overloads skipped). Per unit it computes codeEssence via codeCNFDetailed and resolves each free VALUE ref to one of four §4 classes, ALIGNED to the body's f:idx slots: (a) module-local lifted code-unit -> 'local' edge (edgeKind calls/reads) carrying the target #code: symbol (body emits f:idx); (b) imported name -> 'extern' id extern:<specifier-as-written>#<exportName> derived from the SYNTACTIC import statement, NOT checker module resolution (§5.3 — deterministic with no node_modules); (c) builtin/global -> 'builtin' name; (d) unresolved -> set reducedFidelity. Checker is used for identity resolution ONLY (getSymbolAtLocation + getAliasedSymbol), never inferred types (§5.1). lift() returns CodeUnit[] sorted by symbol (determinism). Exports TS_LENS_VERSION (the exact pinned ts version) for stage 3 to stamp into the essence tag.

lens-registry.name: Lens Registry
lens-registry.description: The code-lens registry (spec §9). lensFor(ext) -> CodeLens | undefined maps a file extension (incl. leading dot) to the responsible lens; v1 registers only TsLens (.ts/.tsx). The single seam future per-language lenses plug into without touching the lift/absorb path.

lift-code-units.name: Lift Code Units
lift-code-units.description: The absorb-side bridge (stage 3a, spec §9 sub-phase 2 / §4.1). liftCodeUnits(rootDir) runs every REGISTERED lens over a read-only worktree root and collects the union of CodeUnits (re-sorted by symbol for deterministic injection order). injectCodeUnits(index, units) turns each CodeUnit into a synthetic SymbolEntry (kind 'component' + componentType 'code-unit'; DETERMINISTIC id = sha256('code:'+symbol), NOT a uuid; source 'premise'; references = the distinct LOCAL targets in first-appearance order so liftEdges yields code->localTarget edges into buildEssenceGraph.adj and Tarjan detects code cycles) and splices it into the live SymbolIndex (entries + byType + bySource) BEFORE computeEssences runs — same universe, never a parallel graph. The identity-bearing payload travels on entry.data: codeEssence (body with positional f:idx slots), codeLocalTargets (the ordered distinct local target symbols the f:N slots substitute against), and essenceTag = "v1:ts"+TS_LENS_VERSION (the compiler-pinned version namespace §5.2, so essence-hash never imports the lens — the tag travels with the node).

absorb.name: Absorb
absorb.description: absorb(gitRef) -> WarpState. Materializes the ref's tree via `git archive | tar` into a temp dir (NO worktree, no .git/worktrees lock — concurrency-safe, T-2026-06-23-003), loadLiveGraph on it, lifts every symbol, builds the WarpState, releaseTree in a finally. The literal WORKTREE ref absorbs the live cwd uncommitted state. STAGE 3a: after loadLiveGraph and before buildWarpState (both the ref and WORKTREE paths), liftCodeUnits + injectCodeUnits splice TS/TSX code-units into the index as synthetic nodes so code essences flow through the same WARP. The lens only READS the worktree/cwd — the read-only invariant holds. DETERMINISM INVARIANT: absorbing the same ref twice is byte-identical (stateId + every per-symbol contentId + repo-relative filePath), so diff(absorb(HEAD), absorb(HEAD)) is provably ZERO. Rests on (a) the absorb root being passed to buildWarpState for repo-relative filePaths, (b) deterministic .purpose/portal file-discovery order in premise-core's aggregator, and (c) the lens's sorted file enumeration + deterministic synthetic ids (duplicate-symbol resolution + Merkle essences are stable across parses regardless of filesystem order or temp-dir prefix).

sem-delta.name: Sem Delta
sem-delta.description: The SemDelta and diff(base, branch), keyed by stableKey (SymbolEntry.id, so rename survives). contentId-equal short-circuits to no-delta; a pure rename/move is the EMPTY delta. Classifies changed contract slots and edge add/remove. A symbol-born delta carries an edgesAdded-only changeset (ALL of the born object's outgoing edges) so a new symbol's outgoing edges feed the dangle pass the same way a gained edge does (born-consumer → retired-target). STAGE 3b: ContractChangeset gains a bodyChanged flag → a 'body' slot in changedSlotsOf. classify sets bodyChanged when either side is a code-unit: classify runs ONLY when contentIds already differ, and a code-unit's identity IS its body (incl. inline-substituted local refs), so a differing code-unit contentId means the body moved. 'body' is the body-INTERNAL analog of 'steps' (a literal/operator change with no call change fires 'body' but not 'edges'; a call add/remove still fires 'edges' via the existing path — both correct). This closes the TD-806 "0 deltas on a .ts-only change" gap.

predict.name: Predict
predict.description: predict(ΔA, ΔB) -> {autoClean, knots[], dangling[]}. The commute / knot / dangle decision procedure. Dangle wins precedence so the score is a true partition; same-key identical-essence is convergent (autoClean). STAGE 3b: 'body' joins the scalar-conflict-slot list (componentType|kind|steps|body) so two branches that edit the SAME code-unit's body to DIFFERENT essences are a KNOT with conflictingSlots ['body'] (git may auto-merge textually-distant edits Warpline flags at function granularity); a call to a code-unit the other branch retired surfaces as a DANGLE via the unchanged edge pass.

justification.name: Justification
justification.description: The v0 Justification — actor/intent from the branch tip's git log, computedRipple via getReferencesTo over changed symbols, danglingRefs, and a reserved signature field (unsigned:sha256 stub).

strand.name: Strand
strand.description: A Strand — one PICK sealed into the fabric. Two deliberately-separated identities: stateId (the REPRODUCIBLE content-address of the meaning it lands on, from #warp-state) and pickId (pick:v0:sha256 over the canonical body — the EVENT identity, including actor + time + intent, so attribution/provenance lives here). Carries a compact StrandDelta (born/retired/contractChanged names + renamedNoop count), an objectCount, git coexistence provenance (ref/treeSha/gitCommit), and calibratedConfidence — RESERVED (null until graded), the one field a git-backed history can't carry and the seed of the non-portable moat. computePickId null-normalizes the body (canonical rejects null) for the ADDRESS only; stored JSON keeps real nulls.

grade.name: Grade
grade.description: The calibration grader (Loid's MOAT — the one thing a git-backed history can't carry). admit SEEDS strand.calibratedConfidence from the gate rule; gradeFabric grades it against real OUTCOME, mirroring the classroom certify→outcome loop. A strand's AUTHORED symbols (delta.born ∪ contractChanged) are OVERTURNED when a later strand RETIRES one (or a #resolve names it in resolves.contended) → confidence ↓; SURVIVED when they hold across a window of later strands → ↑; PENDING when too recent. applyGrades updates calibratedConfidence in the ledger (pickId EXCLUDES the field, so the content-address is unchanged) and appends the trajectory to .warpline/grades.jsonl, under #fabric-lock. The report buckets survival by gate-rule prior class — the falsifiable 'does linked beat independent?' moat experiment.

fabric-lock.name: Fabric Lock
fabric-lock.description: A cross-process advisory lock around the fabric's read-decide-write critical section (Reviewer C1). admit/pick/resolve — and the post-commit auto-seal hook which BACKGROUNDS its seal — can otherwise interleave readSelvage→…→writeSelvage and lose a write (a strand appended that isn't the tip, two strands sharing a seq). withFabricLock acquires an O_EXCL lockfile under .warpline/refs/.lock (atomic create = acquire), bounded retry with backoff, and steals a stale lock (crashed holder) after a TTL. The in-process #repo-lock only guards the git merge-tree fallback; this is the on-disk lock the hook's cross-process seals need.

resolve.name: Resolve
resolve.description: The KNOT council. resolveKnot(root, {agentId, resolvedRef, reason, decidedBy, oursRef?}) seals a HUMAN resolution of a genuine conflict #admit refused to auto-merge: it absorbs the resolved state, records a #strand `resolves` envelope (decidedBy, reason, the contended symbols — precise when --ours is supplied so the original knot is recomputed — and the symbols changed vs the tip), seals via #seal, advances the selvage, and clears the scratch. The reasoning git's merge commit can't keep lives natively in the fabric.

fabric.name: Fabric
fabric.description: The durable Warpline history of this project — the append-only PICK-DAG ledger (.warpline/fabric.jsonl) + the live tip pointer (.warpline/refs/selvage, published atomically via write-tmp+rename so a crash never leaves a half-written tip). readSelvage/writeSelvage/appendStrand/readFabric. COEXISTENCE INVARIANT: writes ONLY under .warpline/ — never the user's git HEAD/index/worktree — extending the Phase-1 ~read-only disk boundary from a debug cache into the authoritative store. Git keeps running normally; Warpline accumulates its OWN meaning-history alongside it.

pick.name: Pick
pick.description: The single-writer WRITE PATH (Phase 2). recordPick(root, opts) absorbs the working tree (or a ref) to a WarpState, and — using the DIFF vs the parent selvage as the source of truth for "did meaning change?" (NOT stateId equality, which hashes the DEDUPED essence set and so misses a born symbol whose essence equals an existing one) — no-ops on an empty diff, else seals a #strand via #seal (the single fabric writer) under #fabric-lock (so a backgrounded post-commit auto-seal can't race it). Genesis (no selvage) records seq 0 with an empty delta; objectCount is the headline. The single-writer daily-driver path — the multi-writer protocol is #admit.

scratch.name: Scratch
scratch.description: A per-agent ephemeral view (the read side of multi-writer). forkScratch(agentId) pins the stateId the agent works against (its optimistic base) under .warpline/refs/scratch/<agentId>; N agents fork the SAME selvage concurrently with zero contention — what git's single shared working-tree/index/HEAD cannot do. Forking is O(1), no working-tree lock. readScratch/clearScratch round it out.

admit.name: Admit
admit.description: The multi-writer WRITE side (Phase C v1, DECISION-level). admitDecision(base, proposed, selvage) is the pure verdict: NOOP (no meaning change); FAST_ADMIT (selvage unadvanced since base → admit directly); CLEAN (selvage advanced but predict(agentΔ, otherΔ) is autoClean — the concurrent edits commute in MEANING, the case git CONFLICTS on for textually-adjacent edits — carrying a GATE-RULE confidence: 'linked' when the two changed-sets are dependency-adjacent in-graph (Merkle would surface a real conflict, so autoClean is trustworthy) vs 'independent' when disjoint (autoClean may HIDE a cross-symbol semantic conflict per the false-AUTOFOLD gate)); KNOT (same symbol, contradictory meaning → human DECIDE, never silently merged); DANGLE (edge into a retired symbol). v2: admit() now PERFORMS the merge — on FAST_ADMIT it seals the proposed state; on CLEAN it calls #materialize to produce the merged tree, seals it, advances selvage, and clears the scratch (if materialization finds a byte conflict the meaning layer missed, it downgrades to KNOT — never a silent wrong-merge). Materialization needs git refs for ours/base/theirs (the strands' provenance.gitCommit anchors); a WORKTREE proposal returns CLEAN unsealed.

merge3.name: Merge3
merge3.description: A token-level 3-way merge (the Phase-C v2 materialization primitive). tokenize splits text into word/whitespace/punct runs (join === text); merge3(base, ours, theirs) does a hunk-based diff3 over token arrays (LCS alignment → change hunks → base-range overlap detection). A range changed by only ONE side takes that side; disjoint changes — even two edits on ONE line, or a deletion next to an edit — compose cleanly (this is what git's LINE-level merge conflicts on). A range BOTH sides changed in OVERLAPPING base coordinates is a CONFLICT (counted; merged then unsafe) — NEVER silently resolved (the VCS cardinal sin). Pure, no I/O.

materialize.name: Materialize
materialize.description: Phase-C v2 meaning→bytes — PERFORM the merge git could only forecast. computeMerge(base, ours, theirs refs) reads each changed file via git (the coexistence byte store) and merges per-file with #merge3; any add/delete-vs-edit or overlapping token-region is a surfaced CONFLICT. materializeMergedState applies the conflict-free plan onto a throwaway copy of the base tree and absorbs it → the merged WarpState (the user's working tree is never touched). gitShow is byte-faithful (no trim) so trailing newlines and exact bytes survive — no drift.

hook.name: Hook
hook.description: The auto-seal git hook. installHook/uninstallHook/hookStatus manage a BEGIN/END-delimited block APPENDED to the repo's post-commit hook (worktree- correct path via gitPath) so every git commit also seals a #strand — the native history accrues in lockstep with git. Coexists with any existing post-commit hook (e.g. Paradigm's history capture), never clobbers it; install is idempotent (refreshes the block in place); uninstall strips only the warpline block. The block seals `--ref HEAD` (the committed tree, never the worktree — so it captures exactly what was committed and never conflates another agent's uncommitted work). Runs in the BACKGROUND (a full-repo absorb is slow) and is fail-safe (`|| true`) so it never delays, blocks, or fails the commit; the strand for commit N lands shortly after N (and rides in N+1).

oracle.name: Oracle
oracle.description: oracle(branchA, branchB) — merge-base → absorb base/A/B → diff → predict → git merge-tree reality (read-only) → score the confusion matrix (agreeClean/agreeConflict/divergeGitOnly/divergeMeaningOnly/score/verdict) → append an OracleRecord to .warpline/oracle.jsonl. The two divergence cells are the experimental result. Conflict paths map to symbols at .purpose-dir level; a git conflict in a NON-SYMBOL file (or an unresolvable merge) becomes gitConflictUnmapped — a git-only divergence that gates the verdict, so the oracle NEVER reads CONVERGENT over a real git conflict (T-2026-06-25-001). The ACTIONABLE answer is a separate mergeClean flag (no knots ∧ no dangling ∧ no git conflict); convergence measures meaning⟷git AGREEMENT, so a contested merge both sides predict scores 'convergent agreement' but is NOT mergeClean — read mergeClean for "is it safe to weave?" (T-2026-06-25-005).

weave.name: Weave
weave.description: The pre-merge MEANING forecast + the semantic-diff report — READ-ONLY and, unlike #oracle, never writes .warpline/. forecast(A, B) reuses the Oracle pipeline up through predict() (mergeBase → absorb base/A/B → diff → predict) and surfaces it as pre-merge UX: a CLEAN-vs-DECISIONS verdict, autoClean count, knots (symbol + contending sides), dangling (from→target, retiredBy). An optional vsGit flag also runs the full Oracle (git merge-tree) read-only for the meaning-vs-bytes divergence comparison. semanticDiff(refA, refB) groups the SemDeltas (born / retired / contract-changed-with-slots / renamed-noop) so the "rename/move is the EMPTY delta" property is visible on real refs. The `weave` WRITE verb is RESERVED, not implemented in Phase 1.

consolidate.name: Consolidate
consolidate.description: The N-way fold FORECAST (read-only) — the N-branch generalization of #weave's forecast(). consolidate(refs[], {base?}) absorbs a common base + N refs IN PARALLEL (concurrency-safe via git-archive materialization, T-2026-06-23-003), diffs each against base, and runs the proven 2-way #predict PAIRWISE across every (i<j), aggregating by symbol: an N-way knot is the union of the pairwise knots on a stableKey (sides = the refs in tension), a dangle is an edge one ref added into a symbol another ref retired, autoFolded = touched keys with no decision. decisions (K_human) = knots + dangles. NO git merge, NO ledger write. The engine behind the falsifiable multi-agent claim (T-2026-06-24-012): a meaning-preserving edit (reorder, local rename) carries ZERO delta and auto-folds where git textually conflicts, so human labor tracks GENUINE meaning-collisions, not branch count. Engine only — no CLI verb wired yet.

lifeline.name: Lifeline
lifeline.description: Meaning-aware blame — lifeline(symbol, {maxCommits}) traces a symbol's ESSENCE through the commits that touched its file (git log --follow, so the thread survives the renames/moves git blame resets on), attributing each essence-change to the commit that INTRODUCED it (newest-first) with the author + INTENT (the commit subject git blame can't show). Resolves the symbol at HEAD, absorbs up to maxCommits of the file history IN PARALLEL (concurrency-safe per T-2026-06-23-003), and emits ONLY genuine meaning changes — a commit that touched the file but not the symbol's meaning is NOT an event. Read-only. MVP: tracks by the ::qualified suffix (rename-stable across file moves; a same-suffix collision elsewhere is a known limitation).

warpline-cli.name: Warpline Cli
warpline-cli.description: The warpline command line (commander). `warpline oracle <a> <b> [--json]`, `warpline absorb <ref> [--json]`, `warpline weave --preview <a> <b> [--vs-git] [--json]` (the pre-merge forecast; the bare `weave` write verb is reserved and refuses with a read-only notice), `warpline consolidate <refs...> [--base R] [--json]` (the N-way fold forecast — CLEAN-to-fold vs N decisions, knots with per-ref sides, dangling, auto-fold count), and `warpline diff [refA] [refB] [--json]` (semantic diff; no args = WORKTREE vs HEAD, one arg = ref vs HEAD, two args = refA vs refB). Plus `warpline status [--json]` (the working tree's MEANING vs HEAD — the named, discoverable form of diff-no-args) and `warpline lifeline <symbol> [--max N] [--json]` (meaning-aware blame — who changed a symbol's meaning, when, why; survives renames). Phase-2 WRITE PATH: `warpline pick [-m <intent>] [--as <actor>] [--confidence <n>] [--ref <ref>] [--quiet] [--json]` seals meaning into the fabric (no-op when unchanged; with `--ref <commit>` and no -m, intent + actor are derived from the commit), `warpline log [--max N] [--json]` shows this project's native meaning-history (the strands, newest first, with the git coexistence anchor), `warpline selvage [--json]` shows the current fabric tip + the strand that sealed it, and `warpline hook <install|uninstall|status>` manages the post-commit auto-seal, `warpline scratch <agentId>` forks a per-agent multi-writer base, `warpline admit <agentId> [--ref <ref>] [--json]` runs the admission protocol (FAST_ADMIT / CLEAN+confidence / KNOT / DANGLE), and `warpline resolve <agentId> --ref <resolvedRef> -m <reason> [--by <who>] [--ours <ref>]` seals a KNOT-council resolution, and `warpline grade [--window N] [--dry] [--json]` grades strand confidence against real survive/overturn outcome (the moat). The only module allowed to write stdout; library code stays quiet.

Wired into orchestrator.ts solo + DAG paths; every call best-effort (a bridge write failure never breaks the CLI run). Imports paradigm-mcp via the established relative-path precedent (core/habits/evaluator.ts).

calibration.name: Calibration

Wired into orchestrator.ts at both per-agent actual sites — faceted (result.relay.metrics.tokens_used, keyed by step.agent + classifyTask(task).type) and solo (agentName + classifyTask(task).type). The estimate itself is NOT recorded (the learned table is actuals-only → no cross-package coupling to the MCP constant). Capture is best-effort — a write failure is logged and swallowed, never alters the run. Aggregated by `paradigm calibrate` into .paradigm/learned/token-estimates.json, which the MCP planner reads learned-first.

calibrate-command.name: Calibrate Command
calibrate-command.description: v7.1 — `paradigm calibrate` aggregation command (the analysis half). Reads .paradigm/events/estimate-actuals.jsonl, groups by (archetype, taskType), and for each group with n>=8 samples computes a robust band (min=p10 of total, max=p90 of total) and writes .paradigm/learned/token-estimates.json as a nested archetype→taskType→band map of {min,max,n}. Groups under the 8-sample floor are NOT written (still use the constant cold-start prior). Reports learned vs. below-floor groups via cli-output helpers (header/kv/success/dim/warn). aggregateActuals + percentile are exported pure functions for testing.

stream-event.name: Stream Event
stream-event.description: Typed Decodable model of the claude --output-format stream-json NDJSON event stream (system/init, system task_started/task_progress/task_updated/task_notification, assistant, user/tool_result, result) — unknown shapes degrade to .unknown rather than throwing. System events route by subtype — task_* subtypes decode into SystemTaskEvent (task lifecycle), all others into SystemInit. SystemTaskEvent decodes the RICH (VERIFIED via live CLI raw capture, 2026-06) task fields — probes id/status/command/output/output_file/tool_use_id/parent_tool_use_id/task_type/description/subagent_type/prompt + the usage block (total_tokens/tool_uses/duration_ms) across flat + nested objects (patch carries task_updated {status,end_time}; usage carries task_notification metrics) — and keeps the full raw JSONValue (logged at debug). CRITICAL — task_* events cover BOTH background bash shells (task_type "local_bash") AND Agent/Task sub-agents (task_type "local_agent"); they emit identical shapes, so task_type is the DETERMINISTIC typing discriminator and tool_use_id is the DETERMINISTIC correlation key consumers use to split bash shells (#atrium-shells) from the sub-agent CHORUS (#sub-agent /

atrium-stop.name: Atrium Stop
atrium-stop.description: Stop control for the ATRIUM composer (#atrium-thread). Visible/enabled ONLY while the agent is mid-turn (status .running/.starting), coral/blocked-tinted stop.fill glyph beside Send. On click calls ClaudeStreamSession.interrupt(), which writes the stream-json CONTROL protocol line {"type":"control_request","request_id":"<uuid>","request":{"subtype":"interrupt"}} to the SAME claude stdin (does NOT close stdin). VERIFIED: the bare {"type":"interrupt"} line is IGNORED (a count-to-600 turn ran to completion); the control_request form halts the active turn (count stopped at 124) and emits {"type":"control_response","response":{"subtype":"success","request_id":"<same>"}} confirming it landed, then the turn ends with a terminal result subtype error_during_execution. The session stays alive; the next user turn is answered normally. interrupt() stops the in-flight caret immediately and tracks the pending request_id; applyControlResponse logs confirmation; applyResult settles status to .idle and treats the interrupt-initiated error_during_execution as a normal 'stopped' (NOT a scary error), with the silence watchdog as backstop. Logged under !claude-interrupt (e.g. 'interrupt control_request sent id=…', 'interrupt CONFIRMED — control_response success').

atrium-shells.name: Atrium Shells
atrium-shells.description: Background-shell inspector for the ATRIUM window. Background shells are commands the agent ran with run_in_background; Claude Code does NOT kill them on session exit (they orphan to PID 1), so the host tracks and reaps them. DETECTION: ClaudeStreamSession parses tool_result text 'Command running in background with ID: <id>' AND 'Output is being written to: <ABSOLUTE>.output' (correlating the command from the matching Bash tool_use id recorded in applyAssistant) AND/OR the system task_started/task_progress/task_updated/task_notification events (task_started gives early registration via task_id + tool_use_id correlation + description; task_updated carries patch.status); results upsert into @Published backgroundShells [BackgroundShell {id, command, startedAt, status running/finished/stopped/killed/failed, lastOutput, outputFile}]. SUB-AGENT FILTER (DETERMINISTIC, task_type-first): task_* events are emitted by BOTH background bash shells (task_type 'local_bash') AND Agent/Task sub-agents (task_type 'local_agent') with identical shapes — only REAL bash shells belong in this panel. On task_started for an untracked id, applySystemTask types by task_type: 'local_agent' routes to the CHORUS (#sub-agent), 'local_bash' admits to this panel; the originating tool_use name (traced via tool_use_id → toolNamesByToolUseId, recorded for EVERY tool_use in applyAssistant) is a FALLBACK only when task_type is absent (older CLI). A present-but-contradicting signal (task_type != local_bash, or fallback tool == 'Agent'/'Task') EXCLUDES the task (logged: 'ignoring non-bash task <id> type=<…> tool=<…>'). The temporal-adjacency FIFO is RETIRED. task_progress is a NON-TERMINAL running heartbeat (the model emits many per task) and is NEVER treated as terminal; only EXPLICIT terminal statuses (killed/stopped/failed/error/finished/completed/success/done/exited) move a shell out of .running — every other value (including empty/absent and progress-ish strings) stays running (the old 'unrecognized non-empty status → failed' rule was removed so progress can't falsely fail a live shell). There are NO pid files (verified) — only the .output file. UI: a right-aligned header button in AtriumThreadView shows a live count/'N live' and opens a popover (AtriumShellsPanel) listing each shell — command (mono, middle-truncated), id, status badge, startedAt, output, and [Inspect]/[Kill] actions; empty state when none. INSPECT (FIX 3, host-side): reads the shell's .output file directly via String(contentsOfFile:), stores it on the shell, and expands the row to a scrollable detail — NO message sent to the agent, NO thread mutation. KILL (FIX B, authoritative): the PRIMARY path is now a SUPPRESSED control turn (ConversationMessage.isControl 'Call the KillShell tool with shell_id <id>…') written to claude's stdin but EXCLUDED from the rendered thread by AtriumThreadView's filter — the agent owns the real task→PID mapping so it kills the CORRECT process. Status is NOT optimistically flipped (the old lsof-on-.output primary killed the file-writer wrapper, the WRONG PID, and LIED 'killed' while the real process lived → later exit 144/SIGURG); instead the real task_updated/task_notification patch.status (→killed/stopped) or the KillShell tool_result drives the panel status so it never lies. A non-authoritative best-effort host SIGTERM via `lsof -t -- <output_file>` remains only as a backstop and never sets the visible status. EXIT CLEANUP: shutdown() best-effort reaps the claude process tree BEFORE terminating claude — collectDescendants via pgrep -P, SIGTERM then SIGKILL survivors after a 300ms grace — preventing the orphan leak. Heavy ConductorLog under !background-shell (detection, raw task payloads, inspect/kill, lsof PIDs, reap).

claude-stream-session.name: Claude Stream Session
claude-stream-session.description: @MainActor ObservableObject owning ONE headless claude process speaking stream-json over stdin/stdout. SPAWN ENVIRONMENT (FIX 1): because Conductor is a Finder-launched GUI/bundled app, it inherits a MINIMAL PATH; the spawned claude would fail to find node/paradigm/hooks (exit 127). loginShellEnvironment() runs the user's login+interactive shell (`$SHELL -lic env`, cached once) and overlays its full environment (PATH + nvm/asdf/homebrew exports) onto the child's environment, with a hardcoded-PATH fallback if the probe fails; the resolved child PATH is logged at startup under #claude-stream-session. Decodes the NDJSON OFF the main thread via a Sendable LineFramer in the readabilityHandler, then hops to @MainActor to project events into the conversation model. Buffers the first turn until system/init; keeps stdin open between turns. Traces every applied event type (system/systemTask/assistant/user/result/unknown) and surfaces claude stderr to ConductorLog so stalls/errors are visible. A silence watchdog settles the UI out of .running if a result is missed (caret off, status idle), and applyResult flips status to idle + records cumulative total_cost_usd and authoritative end-of-turn usage. interrupt() (#atrium-stop) writes the stream-json CONTROL protocol line {"type":"control_request","request_id":"<uuid>","request":{"subtype":"interrupt"}} to the SAME stdin (NOT closed) to halt the active turn while keeping the session alive — the bare {"type":"interrupt"} form is VERIFIED IGNORED. Decodes control_response (applyControlResponse confirms the matching request_id) and settles the interrupt-initiated terminal result (subtype error_during_execution) cleanly as a normal stop, logging under !claude-interrupt. Tracks background shells (#atrium-shells) in @Published backgroundShells by parsing tool_result 'Command running in background with ID: <id>' + 'Output is being written to: <path>' (command correlated from the Bash tool_use id) and system task events; inspectShell reads the .output file host-side; killShell (FIX B) uses the AUTHORITATIVE path — a SUPPRESSED isControl KillShell control turn so the agent kills the correct PID via its task→PID mapping (the old lsof-on-output-file primary targeted the file-writer wrapper, killed the wrong PID, and LIED 'killed' while the process lived) — status is NOT optimistically flipped; the real task_updated/task_notification (patch.status) or KillShell tool_result drives the panel; a non-authoritative best-effort host SIGTERM via lsof remains only as a backstop. shutdown() reaps the claude process tree (pgrep -P → SIGTERM/SIGKILL) before terminating claude to prevent orphan-to-PID-1 leaks.

atrium-theme.name: Atrium Theme
atrium-theme.description: Deep mono visual token system for the ATRIUM thread (void/surface/sunken surfaces, ink, amber/user/tool/running/blocked accents, monospaced body/chip/footer fonts) plus a Color(hex:) initializer.

atrium-thread.name: Atrium Thread
atrium-thread.description: Custom SwiftUI thread surface — a thin top header carrying the background-shell inspector affordance (#atrium-shells), a scrolling conversation pinned to bottom, agent turns with blinking amber caret + collapsible tool chips, right-aligned user capsules, reply composer (ALWAYS editable/focusable — never hard-disabled by session status; Send gated only on live-session + non-empty draft, so a stuck-running turn can never lock the founder out; mid-turn sends queue on claude stdin; a coral Stop button (#atrium-stop) appears beside Send while the agent is mid-turn), and a model·session·tokens·cost footer. THE CHORUS (#atrium-chorus): the body is an HStack of a conversation COLUMN + the right-side CHORUS RAIL using a PUSH layout — when ≥1 sub-agent is live (or the rail is pinned) the column narrows to make room and the rail slides in over 220ms ease (no overlay); it slides away when all sub-agents idle. The conversation column also renders the INLINE FAN-OUT block (#atrium-chorus) after the messages when subAgents is non-empty. Hosted in AtriumSpikeWindow (single-owner of its ClaudeStreamSession), launched from the menu bar — the window is resizable/zoomable/full-screen-capable (collectionBehavior .fullScreenPrimary) with a larger 1100x780 default, built toward the full-screen Conductor.

atrium-chorus.name: Atrium Chorus
atrium-chorus.description: THE CHORUS — sub-agents (#sub-agent) rendered as a chorus of parallel voices, across TWO surfaces over the same @Published subAgents data. SURFACE 1, the INLINE FAN-OUT block (AtriumFanOutBlock): born in the conversation when the model fans out, lists the spawned voices grouped, settles to a one-line summary ('✓ N sub-agents · 2m14s · ▸ expand') when all idle, and lives in history. SURFACE 2, the CHORUS RAIL (AtriumChorusRail): a right-side panel that AUTO-APPEARS while ≥1 sub-agent is live, SLIDES AWAY when all idle, and is PINNABLE (a pin control keeps it open when idle); the conversation column narrows to make room (PUSH layout, 220ms ease, no overlay). ROW ANATOMY (AtriumChorusRow, shared by both surfaces) — prose over mechanics: [state glyph] + TASK DESCRIPTION (system font, ink, leads) + subagent_type (mono, inkMuted, subtitle) + heartbeat SPARKLINE (Canvas, driven by real task_progress ticks) + elapsed (mono, right, ticking via a shared TimelineView clock). TEMPERATURE LAW (founder-baked): running = teal #4ED7A0 (autonomous work needs NO attention — never amber), completed/killed/stopped = inkMuted, failed = coral #FF6B6B, amber #F2B765 ONLY for needsHuman (a sub-agent blocked on the founder; v2 — not yet detected); blue #7CC4FF left-edge = drill/selection focus. SETTLED ROW + DRILL-IN: a settled row shows the status label plus real usage from the terminal task_notification ('done · 12.2k tok · 1.4s'); the inline fan-out summary aggregates tokens across the voices. Clicking a rail row expands it IN PLACE — drill-in shows description + subagent_type + status + elapsed + tokens/tool-uses/duration + the sub-agent prompt + live last-activity. Full nested per-tool transcript is still v2 (interleaved sub-agent tool calls don't yet carry parent_tool_use_id) and is NOT faked. STOP: a rail row's Stop sends a suppressed isControl TaskStop turn (reuses #atrium-shells sendControl); status reflects the real task_updated/notification, not optimistic.

sub-agent.name: Sub Agent
sub-agent.description: Observable record of a sub-agent the model spawned via the Agent/Task tool for parallel work (THE CHORUS, #atrium-chorus). SubAgent {id (taskId), description, subagentType, status (running/completed/stopped/killed/failed/needsHuman), startedAt, endedAt, lastActivity, progressTicks (sparkline heartbeats), originatingToolUseId, prompt, totalTokens, toolUses, durationMs; usageSummary computed → '12.2k tok · 1.4s'}. TYPING + CORRELATION ARE DETERMINISTIC (corrected 2026-06 from the earlier wrong temporal-adjacency conclusion): task_* events carry task_type ('local_agent' → sub-agent; 'local_bash' → bash shell) AND tool_use_id (ties the task to the EXACT spawning Agent tool_use) — the temporal-adjacency FIFO is RETIRED. POPULATION (ClaudeStreamSession @Published subAgents): an Agent/Task tool_use in applyAssistant caches description/subagent_type/prompt in agentSpawnsByToolUseId keyed by tool_use_id (FALLBACK only). applySystemTask routes a task to the chorus instead of the shells panel (#atrium-shells) when task_type == 'local_agent' (or, on an old CLI with no task_type, the originating tool is Agent/Task). applySubAgentTask populates the SubAgent DIRECTLY from the task_started fields (description + subagent_type + prompt — all on the event), sets originatingToolUseId from the event's tool_use_id, appends a sparkline tick per task_progress, updates lastActivity, captures usage (total_tokens/tool_uses/duration_ms) from the terminal task_notification via applyUsage, and freezes the sub-agent (endedAt) on terminal task_updated/notification. STATUS: 'completed' maps to .completed → muted ✓ (terminal SUCCESS, distinct from .killed/.stopped/.failed). parent_tool_use_id is still probed for forward-compat (interleaved sub-agent tool-call attribution → full nested drill-in, v2). subAgentTaskIds is sticky so signal-less follow-up events stay routed to the chorus. stopSubAgent sends a suppressed isControl TaskStop turn (authoritative; real status drives the UI). Bash shells (#atrium-shells) stay a SEPARATE list.

atrium-attachment.name: Atrium Attachment
atrium-attachment.description: Removable file-attachment chip for the ATRIUM composer — file-type SF Symbol + middle-truncated filename + ✕ remove, styled to the ATRIUM palette (surfaceRaised bg, tool-violet icon, mono ink filename). Files dragged onto the composer (.onDrop of .fileURL) become chips in a row above the field; on send the absolute paths are appended to the outgoing claude -p turn as a trailing "Attached files:" block so the agent can Read them, while the visible draft stays clean.

atrium-voice.name: Atrium Voice
atrium-voice.description: Keyword-driven voice dictation loop for the ATRIUM composer, modeled on a-aloud's reply-window loop. REUSES WhisperVoiceProvider (WhisperKit CoreML STT + AVCaptureSession mic) — no new STT dependency. Mic-button path AUTHORIZES FIRST — checks AVCaptureDevice.authorizationStatus(for:.audio), on .notDetermined awaits requestAccess (fires the TCC prompt; Info.plist has NSMicrophoneUsageDescription), on .denied/.restricted surfaces a `blocked` state whose next click opens System Settings › Privacy › Microphone — THEN loads the WhisperKit model (`loading` state) and starts continuous capture. State machine off→requesting→loading→armed→composing→sending→armed (+blocked) driven by forgiving word-boundary-anchored keyword grammar (normalize, last-occurrence match, multi-word phrases). Keywords are USER-CONFIGURABLE in Settings › Input › "Voice Composer (ATRIUM)" and persist in UserDefaults (atriumWakeKeyword / atriumSendKeyword / atriumCancelKeywords — cancel is a comma-separated list); they are re-read fresh at each arm (loadAndArm → refreshKeywordsFromDefaults) so a Settings change takes effect on the next arm. Defaults (seeds + fallbacks) wake="respond", send="send it", cancel="scratch that, never mind, nevermind". Uses its OWN WhisperVoiceProvider instance — fully decoupled from the orchestrator's global `voiceEnabled` pref, so the explicit mic-button action starts regardless of that setting. Live transcript streams into the composer's NSTextView via the

atrium-textview.name: Atrium Textview
atrium-textview.description: Custom NSViewRepresentable (AtriumTextView) wrapping an NSTextView subclass (AtriumNSTextView) in an NSScrollView — the ATRIUM composer's reply input. Multiline, grows to ~6 lines then scrolls. ATRIUM styling (surface bg, ink text, monospaced 13, amber insertion point + selection). Two-way bound to the composer's draft via a Coordinator (textDidChange → binding); imperative AtriumTextViewHandle exposes appendText/clear/focus for the voice dictation path. pack-loader.description: v6.0 (v5.39.0 sub-phase 1) multi-tenant content-pack discovery + resolution. loadPackManifest reads pack.yaml via safeLoad (classifier-only errors — never leaks file contents). discoverPacks scans three sources in precedence order: (1) node_modules/@a-company/university, (2) direct-deps with paradigm.universityPack pointer in package.json, (3) local .paradigm/university/ + discipline sub-packs. resolveEntryAddress parses <pack-id>:<entry-id> or bare ids; bare ids throw ambiguity errors when present in multiple active packs. Cache at .paradigm/cache/packs.json keyed by node_modules + local-university mtimes so npm install / local edits invalidate automatically. v6.5: synthesizes an implicit default `main` section for packs that omit `sections:` (back-compat path that keeps v6.4 packs rendering pixel-identical); validates declared sections against the Section Zod schema; surfaces sections[] on every loaded pack so search/list/UI can route by section.

university-metrics.name: University Metrics

Honors config.metrics.local_snapshots_enabled (no-op when false). loadRecentSnapshots returns newest-first slice. pruneOldSnapshots removes files older than 90 days (default). computeProjectSaltHash creates/reads .paradigm/.metrics-salt with 0o600 perms; salt is 32 bytes of crypto.randomBytes. Feeds v6.3 sunset review per spec §8.

wisdom-loader.name: Wisdom Loader

Global wisdom merged from ~/.paradigm/wisdom/ (local wins on id collision). v5.39.0 sub-phase 1: emits a one-time deprecation warning when .paradigm/wisdom/decisions/ still contains YAML files, pointing at `paradigm migrate decisions` (v6.0). injects a decision-time orchestration directive into model context, once
per TTL window, telemetry on every match) and team-gate (PreToolUse
Write|Edit; one-time stderr advisory before source edits in unresolved
sessions). Both honor .orchestrated / fresh .solo-declared markers and
the PARADIGM_TEAM_GATE=off kill switch. Markers expire by AGE
(PARADIGM_GATE_TTL_HOURS, default 4h) — never stop-cleared, because Stop
fires per assistant turn. Check 13 in paradigm-common.sh records deduped
bypass events to team-funnel telemetry at both warn and block severity.

check-14-remediation-gate.name: Check 14 Remediation Gate
check-14-remediation-gate.description:
v6.1 Sprint 1 Wave 2 — Stop hook Check 14. Iterates the cached
_REMEDIATIONS_JSON (sourced from `paradigm internal active-remediations
--json`). severity=guard adds to VIOLATIONS (blocks); advise/auto-author
route to ADVISORY. Honors PARADIGM_OVERRIDE comma-list to skip ids and
append an audit row to .paradigm/events/overrides.jsonl with mechanism=env.
Iteration uses temp-file + redirect (NOT pipe) for POSIX subshell-safe
VIOLATION_COUNT propagation.

WarplineSection.name: WarplineSection
WarplineSection.description: Warpline section shell (sub-phase 2) — the Oracle Divergence Viewer. Lays out the OracleLedgerRail (left) beside the OracleDivergenceViewer (right). On mount fetches GET /api/warpline/ledger?limit=200 (selecting the newest row) and GET /api/warpline/refs (for the picker). Run posts /api/warpline/oracle (records → prepends + selects) and Preview posts /api/warpline/forecast {vsGit:true} (ephemeral, adapted via forecastToRecord, never added to the rail). Subscribes to the `warpline-ws` CustomEvent (forwarded by useAgentEffects from the `warpline:*` server broadcast) — on `warpline:oracle-record-appended` it prepends the new record (deduped by rowKey) so a live run repaints without a poll. All read-only; the UI never constructs a write/weave call.

OracleLedgerRail.name: OracleLedgerRail
OracleLedgerRail.description: Left rail — a RefPicker (two branch <select>s sourced from /refs + Run/Preview buttons) above the /ledger list rendered newest-first. Each row shows branchA→branchB (ledgerRowLabel) · verdict · ts; DIVERGENT rows (isDivergentRow) carry a seam-violet dot. Clicking a row selects it (rowKey identity) → drives the viewer. Run is disabled until two distinct branches are picked.

OracleDivergenceViewer.name: OracleDivergenceViewer
OracleDivergenceViewer.description: THE screen where "git sees bytes, Warpline sees meaning" is the whole page. Composes RunHeader (branchA ◀ weave ▶ branchB + mergeBase + ts), MeaningVsBytesSplit (the hero — a hard 50/50 split: LEFT bytes/git monospace with a CLEAN ✓ / CONFLICT chip off gitReality.conflicted; a 1px center violet SEAM that pulses on headline divergence; RIGHT meaning/warp serif with a DIVERGENT/CLEAN chip off convergence.verdict + knot/dangle tally), ConfusionMatrix (a literal 2×2 git×meaning whose 4 cells bind convergence.{agreeClean,divergeGitOnly,divergeMeaningOnly,agreeConflict}; each cell clickable to expand its real symbol keys; the divergeMeaningOnly cell is the ★, the only cell that glows — static box-shadow, never animated, no count-up), VerdictCard (verdict + score ALWAYS beside the raw agree/git-only/ meaning-only counts + a templated consequence line from dangling[0] or knots[0]) and DivergencePanel (a KnotRender per prediction.knots — two intent threads A=--warp/B=--weft cinching a knot glyph, conflictingSlots incl. the code-lens 'body' slot; a DangleRender per prediction.dangling — a severed thread drifting into a dashed violet void labeled danglingTargetSymbol + retiredBy). CONVERGENT/empty renders the calm "No knots. No dangles. The weave is clean." Includes a basic DrillDown slide-over (knot essenceA/essenceB + slots, or dangle from→target). All four hero states are chosen purely from real OracleRecord fields (heroState).

warpline-viewer-state.name: Warpline Viewer State
warpline-viewer-state.description: The React-free PURE binding layer (viewerState.ts). Maps real OracleRecord fields onto UI decisions: heroState (the 4-state mood), isHeadlineDivergence (divergeMeaningOnly>0 — lights the ★ + pulses the seam), gitChip/meaningChip, matrixCells (the literal 2×2 with per-cell symbol keys + the ★ flag), rawCounts, consequenceLine (dangle-first templated line), isCalm + CALM_DIVERGENCE_COPY, ledgerRowLabel/isDivergentRow/rowKey, knotDrill/dangleDrill, and forecastToRecord (adapts a vsGit Forecast to an ephemeral OracleRecord for Preview). Unit-tested in a node env (viewerState.test.ts) against a DIVERGENT and a CONVERGENT sample — keeps "the number can't lie" falsifiability a pure asserted function.

warpline-web-types.name: Warpline Web Types
warpline-web-types.description: types.ts — a structural mirror of the engine's exported shapes (OracleRecord, Knot, Dangle, Justification, Convergence, GitReality) plus RefsResponse. Field names track @a-company/warpline VERBATIM; the platform-ui is a separate Vite package so it re-declares the read-only fields the viewer binds rather than importing the engine. The dangle target is read from danglingTargetSymbol (the engine's real field), presented as the "target essence" the spec describes.

TasksSection.name: TasksSection
TasksSection.description: Tasks section shell in Platform UI — header band (title + live "{n} open · {n} in-flight · {n} unclaimed" stat off board.summary) and a Board|List|Inbox ViewSwitcher. Defaults to Board. The Board renders a four-tab sub-tab bar (BoardTabs: State | Claimant | Symbol/Flow | Calibration, State default). The three lane tabs render the FilterBar + BoardView (grouped by boardTab) with the lanes filling full viewport height; the Calibration tab renders the full-area calibration grid (CalibrationStrip variant='tab') with NO FilterBar and NO lanes. List renders the ListView; Inbox the InboxView. 10s section-guarded poll drives fetchTasks + fetchBoard + fetchCalibration. Also subscribes to the `tasks-ws` CustomEvent (forwarded from the central WS hub useAgentEffects, which relays tasks:* server broadcasts) — on tasks:synced / tasks:sync-conflict it refreshes fetchBoard()+fetchTasks()(+inbox) so poll-driven reconciliations appear live without a user click.

TaskCard.name: TaskCard
TaskCard.description: Card cloning the lore-card structure — priority + status chips, line-clamped title, the prominent CalibrationBlock, a claimant chip colored via the shared AGENT_COLORS map, a fragile/symbol tag row, and a GitHub badge when external_ref.provider is github. When a card has no actual claimant but carries a proposedClaimant (Cid's suggested owner on unclaimed tasks), it renders a subtle dashed "→ {ref}" hint in that claimant's color — distinct from a real claim chip. Round D — clickable (onClick → store.openDetail(id), keyboard-accessible), an optional elevated `hero` variant for the Inbox, and live agent-effect registration via useTaskAgentEffect (symbol-matched pulse/color/label + badge stamps; keyed by taskId so the 10s poll re-render doesn't detach the highlight).

CalibrationBlock.name: CalibrationBlock
CalibrationBlock.description: The calibration moat made visible. SIZE tracks confidence — learned estimates lead with a big (32px) green Fibonacci story-point + a green LEARNED badge (◆ + n{count}); prior cold-start guesses LEAD with the dimmed italic ~prior~ label and demote the number to a recessed ~17px secondary value so a guess never out-shouts a learned band. Both render the raw token band plus a small muted cell caption (claimant-archetype × taskType, e.g. "builder×feature") mapping the estimate back to the calibration grid.

tasksStore.name: TasksStore
tasksStore.description: Zustand store for the Tasks section (mirrors loreStore). Holds list, board, calibration, inbox, detail, filter, boardTab and dep-cache state, each fetch with its own AbortController; default view is board. boardTab is the Board's sub-tab ('state' default | 'claimant' | 'symbol' | 'calibration'), persisted to localStorage key paradigm.tasks.boardTab with graceful migration from the legacy paradigm.tasks.laneMode key; setBoardTab updates it. BoardView derives its laneMode from boardTab for the three lane tabs. Read fetches hit the /api/tasks read routes; Task/BoardNode/BoardUnclaimed carry the computed estimate + taskType. The UI's ONLY write verbs live here — claimTask, startTask, doneTask, blockTask, unblockTask all POST the enforced /api/tasks/:id action endpoints (which proxy the updateTask state machine), and syncGitHub posts /api/tasks/sync for two-way reconcile; each refreshes board/list/inbox on success and surfaces a transient actionError/sync summary. BoardData also carries the three optional Cid/Loid governance detections (integrity, settlementDebt, staleClaims) passed through to BoardHealth.

TaskActions.name: TaskActions
TaskActions.description: Shared status-aware write-verb row rendered by both the InboxView hero and the TaskDetailPanel header — the single mutation surface in the Tasks UI. Respects the v7 task state machine so it never offers a verb that would 409 — open → [Start] + [Claim to me] (shown only when unclaimed or already held by the viewer; passes the human ref from /whoami, kind:'human') + [Done] + [Block]; in-progress → [Done] + [Block]; done/shelved are terminal (no verbs); blocked_on set → a reason banner + [Unblock] (orthogonal to status). Block opens a window.prompt for the reason. Wires each button to the matching tasksStore action and renders store.actionError as a dismissable inline error (e.g. the 409 "cannot displace a human/peer claim"). Buttons disable while an action is in flight.

storyPoints.name: StoryPoints
storyPoints.description: Pure helper tokenBandToPoints({min,max}) → Fibonacci story point (1/2/3/5/8/13/21) by mapping the band midpoint through tunable token thresholds (POINT_THRESHOLDS), to be re-fit against real actuals later.

board-utils.name: Board Utils
board-utils.description: Board helpers — AGENT_COLORS (verbatim from TeamSection) + claimantColor() which resolves a claimant ref to its Team color via a CLAIMANT_ALIAS map (cid→architect, forge→builder, compliance→security; role words map to themselves) so a claimant's lane color === their Team color, with a widened hashed-fallback (S/L jitter) keeping unknown refs mutually distinct; claimantArchetype() exposes the same ref→archetype resolution for calibration-cell matching. Plus deriveSymbols()/firstSymbol() (tags + blurb-parsed

BoardView.name: BoardView
BoardView.description: Horizontally-scrollable row of SwimLanes off /api/tasks/board, filling full viewport height (each lane's card column scrolls internally). The lane mode is derived from the active board sub-tab (boardTab): laneMode='state' (the default tab) = open/in-progress/done/shelved kanban; 'claimant' = one lane per claimant.ref + trailing Unclaimed lane (hidden entirely when 0 cards) + collapsed Done lane; 'symbol' = grouped by each card's first derived symbol. Honors store status/priority/search + calibrationFilter — the cell filter matches the task's real taskType field against the cell column and the claimant's resolved archetype against the cell row; a 0-match cell click shows a specific "No {taskType} tasks claimed by {archetype} yet" empty state. Renders the BoardHealth advisory banner above the lanes — it self-hides when the board carries no governance detections. The lane sub-tab bar lives in TasksSection (BoardTabs), not here.

BoardHealth.name: BoardHealth
BoardHealth.description: Compact collapsible ADVISORY banner at the top of BoardView surfacing the three Cid/Loid governance detections the backend attaches to the board — integrity (DAG defects: self-parent / dangling / cycle), settlementDebt (children all terminal but the epic never settled), and staleClaims (archetype-claimed open tasks past 7 days). Amber, never error-red, never blocking. Self-hides entirely when the board is healthy. Collapsed by default to a count summary (persisted to localStorage); expanded it lists each detection grouped by kind, and clicking a row with a taskId opens that task's detail panel.

SwimLane.name: SwimLane
SwimLane.description: Single vertical board lane — colored header (label + presence dot + card count + SUMMED story points) using AGENT_COLORS, a scrollable column of TaskCards sorted in-progress-first then priority-desc, collapsible via chevron with per-lane localStorage persistence.

BoardTabs.name: BoardTabs
BoardTabs.description: The Board's sub-tab bar — four tabs in order State | Claimant | Symbol/Flow | Calibration (State is the default), styled with the shared segmented .view-tab idiom. Active tab = store.boardTab; clicking sets boardTab via setBoardTab. Replaces the old LaneModeToggle pill.

FilterBar.name: FilterBar
FilterBar.description: Tasks filter bar lifted from lore's pattern — status dropdown, priority dropdown, search-blurb input wired to store filter state, plus a clearable active-filter chip surfacing the calibrationFilter (archetype×taskType) when set.

CalibrationStrip.name: CalibrationStrip
CalibrationStrip.description: The calibration moat surface off /api/tasks/calibration, with two rendering modes via a variant prop. variant='tab' (the Calibration sub-tab, current usage): a coverage header ("{pct}% calibrated cells · {graduated} of {total} graduated") + the full CellGrid filling the available height (scrolls when tall), with no collapse chrome; on cold-start it shows a "learning in progress" badge + the "Run `paradigm calibrate`…" CTA. Clicking a cell sets the calibrationFilter AND switches boardTab to 'state' so the filtered lanes show. variant='strip' (legacy) is the default-ON collapsible hero strip above the board — coverage StatCard + CellGrid, collapse persisted to localStorage with a glanceable collapsed summary, force-expanded on full cold-start so the differentiated artifact never starts hidden.

CellGrid.name: CellGrid
CellGrid.description: Calibration matrix — archetype rows × taskType columns. Learned cells render solid + agent-color tint + a ● dot + compact band ("3–13" n24); PRIOR cells encode progress-to-graduation (a cell graduates at n>=8) as a live ramp — fill width + cell opacity + border tint ramp by min(n,8)/8 toward the archetype color, and an in-cell "{n}/8" tick reads the sample count directly, so a cell accumulating actuals (n=5) looks visibly closer to graduating than an empty one (n=0). The grid answers "where is the team about to learn something," not just "nothing yet." Clicking a cell toggles the store calibrationFilter that BoardView honors and FilterBar surfaces as a chip; an optional onCellSelect callback fires when a cell is selected (used by the Calibration tab to switch back to the State lanes).

InboxView.name: InboxView
InboxView.description: The Inbox tab — the AGENT FACE. A claimant pill-row (a "Me" pill resolved via /api/tasks/whoami + one AGENT_COLORS-tinted pill per distinct board claimant) selects whose inbox to focus via fetchInbox(kind, ref). The focused column shows a rolled-up calibration header ("calibration {pct}% · n={total}", share of source==='learned') — suppressed to "—" for human claimants, whose learned bands are archetype-keyed so a % would be a category error, a NEXT-ACTIONABLE hero card (highest-priority in-progress-or-open, not blocked) elevated on top, a DependsChain ribbon under the hero (●done → ●this → ○next) that resolves each dependsOn id first from the loaded board/inbox pool (now incl. board.loose) and, for cross-run ids not in that pool, lazily via store.resolveDep → GET /api/tasks/:id (deduped + cached in store.depCache; a cached null = a genuine 404) so deps render "unknown" only after a fetch truly fails rather than for any out-of-pool id, then the rest as a queued list of TaskCards. Cold-start default landing is the human's ("Me") inbox; empty claimants render "inbox zero". Round E renders a TaskActions row directly under the hero card so the valid write verbs (start/claim/done/block) act from the agent face.

GitHubSyncStrip.name: GitHubSyncStrip
GitHubSyncStrip.description: Persistent Board-tab footer. Aggregates external_ref state across visible board tasks — synced (provider==='github' && url) and push-pending (github && no url), both derived from real external_ref state (the always-0 "drifted" placeholder was dropped as less honest than its absence). The PRIMARY action is now a REAL two-way Sync button (Round F) — on click it calls store.syncGitHub() → POST /api/tasks/sync (no client body; the server pulls each linked GitHub issue and reconciles it back through the enforced state machine, 100% server-side) and disables with a spinner ("Syncing…") while in flight. On return it renders a transient inline summary off store.lastSyncSummary in one of three tones — success ("✓ Synced N · M unchanged" in green; a quiet "Up to date" on a 0-change result); CONFLICT (amber --p-accent-amber, never error-red — conflict means local won and a human should look — with the conflicted task ids as clickable chips → store.openDetail(id)); OFFLINE (calm "GitHub not available — `gh auth login` to enable sync" hint when every verdict is offline/skipped or the request failed, NOT a red failure). After a sync that applied changes the store re-runs fetchBoard()+fetchTasks()(+fetchInbox if a claimant is focused) so changes show immediately. A small "via CLI" SECONDARY affordance remains — opens a popover that clipboard-copies `paradigm task sync` as a fallback for users without the server. The client never sends task/remote state.

TaskDetailPanel.name: TaskDetailPanel
TaskDetailPanel.description: Right-slide detail panel cloning lore's .detail-overlay/.detail-panel. Opened by clicking any TaskCard (store.openDetail(id)); fetches GET /api/tasks/:id (seeded instantly from the already-loaded board/inbox/list pool). Shows full blurb, the dependsOn DAG (ids + resolved states), the estimate breakdown (token band + LEARNED/prior provenance + n), fragileSymbols/tags chips, a GitHub section (ref + link when url present), and related_lore ids. Round E renders a TaskActions row in the header area so the write verbs work from any view (board/list click → detail → act); the panel re-seeds its local task from the refreshed store pool after a verb so the status-aware action row updates without a manual refetch. Closes on backdrop click / Esc.

useTaskAgentEffect.name: UseTaskAgentEffect
useTaskAgentEffect.description: Hook consuming the shared agentStore the SAME way the platform's agent-effect protocol works — matched by SYMBOL (not taskId). A card registers its derived symbols (board.deriveSymbols) and intersects them against agentStore.highlights[].symbols (pulse + color + label) and agentStore.annotations of type 'badge' (symbol-targeted badge stamps). Mute clears agentStore, so a muted session yields no card effects for free.

DocsSection.name: DocsSection
DocsSection.description: Documentation browser in Platform UI — sidebar navigation, symbol pages, flow diagrams, portal reference

help-view.name: Help View
help-view.description: In-app help system with 9-section guide covering Conductor capabilities, menus, shortcuts, and known limitations. Accessible via ? button.

agent-decision.name: Agent Decision
agent-decision.description: Model for a host-rendered branching CHOICE the agent offers the human ($decision-exchange), parsed from a conductor-decision fenced block (#fenced-block-parser). Carries question + 2-5 DecisionOptions (label/description/★recommended/▸visualId/affectedSymbols) + multiSelect/allowOther + an optional top-level `symbols` array (the real graph symbols the decision is about) + an optional settled DecisionAnswer. symbols/affectedSymbols default [] (schema-tolerant) and drive the hover-to-spotlight binding into the LIGHTBOX graph. composeReply() builds the human-readable user turn. Lives on ConversationMessage (additive).

agent-visual.name: Agent Visual
agent-visual.description: Model for a host-rendered DIAGRAM, COMPARISON or GRAPH ($decision-exchange), parsed from a conductor-visual envelope or a bare mermaid/svg fence (#fenced-block-parser). kind flow|comparison|graph render in v1 (LIGHTBOX); graph carries a GraphPayload (root/nodes/edges/truncated/freshness) drawn by #atrium-graph-view; wireframe|diff are decode-tolerant v2 placeholders. Rendered as a ▸ launcher chip — never auto-opens.

atrium-decision-card.name: Atrium Decision Card
atrium-decision-card.description: Inline card rendering an #agent-decision in the ATRIUM thread. PENDING = question + stacked radio/checkbox option cards + Other… field (when allowOther) + escape affordances, AMBER leading rail (Mika's temperature law); on pick calls onAnswer → ClaudeStreamSession.answerDecision. ANSWERED = collapsed teal ✓ you chose <label> with a change/reopen affordance. ★ marks a recommended lean; ▸ view opens a linked visual in the LIGHTBOX. Hovering an option row fires onHoverSymbols(option.affectedSymbols) (empty on hover-out) → spotlights those symbols in the LIGHTBOX graph (#atrium-graph-view); READ-ONLY — clicking is still the only commit path.

atrium-visual-canvas.name: Atrium Visual Canvas
atrium-visual-canvas.description: THE LIGHTBOX — a 380pt right slide-out hosting one #agent-visual. Shares the right zone with the CHORUS rail and renders OVER it (chorus stays mounted; PUSH-consistent layout, conversation column narrows). Switches on kind: flow → MermaidWebView (sandboxed offline WKWebView, vendored mermaid.min.js, NO network, ATRIUM-recolored); comparison → native SwiftUI table (ATRIUM styling); graph → #atrium-graph-view (❖ header glyph); wireframe/diff → v2 placeholder. Takes a plain `highlightedSymbols: Set<String>` (NOT folded into the Equatable #agent-visual) and forwards it to #atrium-graph-view for the decision-option hover spotlight — kept separate so hover only redraws the Canvas, never re-identifies the LIGHTBOX.

atrium-graph-view.name: Atrium Graph View
atrium-graph-view.description: Native SwiftUI Canvas render of a bounded symbol ego-graph (#agent-visual kind == .graph) inside THE LIGHTBOX. STATIC closed-form RING layout: root (focus) at center with a soft halo, other nodes evenly on a ring (angle 2π·i/count, radius shrunk to fit 380pt). Edges draw under nodes as center→ring lines. Node shapes encode GraphSymbolKind via Mika's accent mapping (component→ink rounded rect, flow→user stadium, gate→amber diamond, signal→teal circle, aspect→violet dashed). Labels = symbol id, scaled off atriumFontScale. Footer shows +N-more (truncated) + stale-index. HOVER SPOTLIGHT (Phase-2c): a plain `highlightedSymbols: Set<String>` (driven by decision-option hover) lights matching nodes at full saturation + a brighter amber ring and DIMS all others to ~40% (edges between two lit nodes draw amber); an animated dimPhase eases the room dim in/out over ~150ms on hover-in/out. READ-ONLY — never selects/commits; an empty set renders at rest. NO force sim, drag, or zoom.

mermaid-web-view.name: Mermaid Web View
mermaid-web-view.description: Sandboxed WKWebView that renders a mermaid diagram OFFLINE from a vendored mermaid.min.js (Resources/, loaded via #conductor-resources to dodge the SwiftTerm Bundle.module collision). nil baseURL, navigation blocked except the in-memory load, ATRIUM dark theme. Degrades to a source dump if the script is missing from the bundle.

cockpit-view.name: Cockpit View
cockpit-view.description: THE BRIDGE root — HSplitView { FleetSpineView | center }. Center renders the active session's AtriumThreadView with `.id(active.id)` (load-bearing), 120ms cross-fade in place on switch, else the calm FleetEmptyState. Hosts ⌘1–9 / ⌘↑↓ / ⌘N fleet shortcuts and the spawn sheet.

fleet-spine.name: Fleet Spine
fleet-spine.description: Left spine — a bridge bar ('N sessions · M needs you', amber when M>0, 'all calm' when M==0) over a status-grouped session list: NEEDS YOU (always first, not collapsible, hidden when empty), WORKING, IDLE (auto-collapse past 1). Density tiers compact WORKING/IDLE rows past 6/9 sessions; NEEDS YOU rows never compact. `+ new session` at bottom.

session-row.name: Session Row
session-row.description: One session in the spine (mirrors AtriumChorusRow): status glyph (animated for running/awaitingYou) · prose projectName · mono model·age subtitle · one-line italic last-activity preview · status·~tokens micro-signal. Active row = blue left-edge + surfaceRaised fill; awaitingYou keeps an amber edge + faint pulsing wash. Hover/active reveals a close affordance.

session-spawn-sheet.name: Session Spawn Sheet
session-spawn-sheet.description: Sheet over the dimmed cockpit — ProjectStore.sorted recents + an NSOpenPanel 'Browse…' folder picker + an optional opening-prompt field. oracle-run.name: Oracle Run

~read-only.name: ~read Only
~read-only.description: THE GIT-SAFETY INVARIANT (Phase-1 read-only; PRESERVED by the Phase-2 write path) — Warpline NEVER mutates the user's git HEAD/index/worktree. A ref is read by materializing its tree via `git archive` into a throwaway temp dir (no worktree, no .git/worktrees lock); the cold git<2.38 merge-tree fallback uses a detached worktree torn down in a finally. The ONLY disk Warpline writes is under .warpline/ — the content-addressed store, the oracle.jsonl ledger, AND the Phase-2 native history (#fabric: refs/selvage + fabric.jsonl + states/). The write path is a write to Warpline's OWN store, NOT to git: git is read for provenance (HEAD sha, user.name) only. Lifting a ref, or the WORKTREE pseudo-ref, only READS files — the code-lens included.

~determinism.name: ~determinism
~determinism.description: THE THESIS — absorbing the same ref twice is byte-identical (stateId + every per-symbol contentId + repo-relative filePath), so diff(absorb(HEAD), absorb(HEAD)) is provably ZERO and two machines on the same source agree. No timestamps/paths/positions/prose/embeddings enter the hashed byte stream; every set is sorted+deduped; strict canonical JSON; sorted file enumeration; deterministic synthetic code-unit ids; the TS compiler is exact-pinned and stamped into the code essence tag (essence:v1:ts<exact>) so a different compiler is a different content-address namespace, never a silent collision.

~meaning-coverage.name: ~meaning Coverage
~meaning-coverage.description: THE TD-806 HONESTY METRIC — Warpline reports WHERE it has meaning versus where it degrades to opaque bytes (the 3-tier fidelity model). A code-unit the TS lens cannot soundly lift (unresolved refs, unsupported forms) is flagged reducedFidelity — never silently empty; coverage is surfaced, not assumed. Honest about its own blind spots so the meaning layer's thickness is legible.
